trap_note: lb (mass) vs lbf (force) are different quantities
Datasheets often write "kg" when they mean kgf
Hobby load cells/springs quote "g" meaning gram-force
"oz" on a force spec means ozf = lbf/16
Hobby servo/stepper "kg.cm" or "kg-cm" means kgf*cm; 1 kgf*cm ~ 0.098 N*m (not 1 N*m and not 0.01)
"oz-in" on servo/stepper specs = ozf*in; 1 oz-in ~ 7.06 mN*m
Motor rotor inertia "g.cm2" is a mass*length^2 (not gf); 1 g*cm^2 = 1e-7 kg*m^2
CAD mass properties often report kg*mm^2 or g*mm^2
US motor catalogs give inertia in oz-in-s^2 (force-based); numerically equals oz-in torque factor
Battery capacity; energy = mAh * V * 3.6 J
Servo speed spec "0.12 s/60deg" is a TIME per 60 deg: omega = factor / value (inverse!), not value*factor
Affine: K = degC + 273.15 (temperature DIFFERENCES use factor only)
